messages:
Alyssa Chen: Heads-up — AcmeCorp just escalated: same query set before/after our rerank model update showing big score swings, customers seeing reorders in prod :eyes:
Acme Support: Confirmed — we replayed 50 golden queries and 12 had >0.2 absolute score change, several moved from top-1 to top-3. This started right after the 2026-03-10 rerank deployment (rerank-v2.1.3).
Ben Ortiz: Can you paste an example input + two responses (old vs new) so SRE/ML can repro?
Acme Support: Sure, here's one. POST /v1/rerank body:
```
{
  "query": "wireless earbuds noise cancelling comparison",
  "candidates": [
    "BrandX model A - great ANC",
    "BrandY model B - budget",
    "BrandZ model C - midsize battery"
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```
Old scores (pre-2026-03-10): [0.918, 0.754, 0.483]
New scores (post-2026-03-10): [0.634, 0.812, 0.591]
Acme Support: Note: same request id, same ordering, no truncation.
Jamal Reed: Hmm. That looks like a model-side calibration/regression rather than input formatting. Any chance tokenization or prompt prefix changed in the rollout?
Ben Ortiz: I checked the release diff — we changed attention scaling for some layers and switched to int8 quant path for TFL backend on certain GPU types. Patch: "optimize/quant-int8-switch" landed in the canary.
Sara Martinez: Deploy Bot: "Canary deployment started for rerank-v2.1.3 on shard us-west-2-c (10% traffic)" :robot_face:
Alyssa Chen: We need repro steps for engineers. Acme — can you run this curl snippet against both /v1/rerank? One hitting canary model endpoint, one hitting pinned older model?
Acme Support: Will do. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '@payload.json' -- show-request-id
Acme Support: Results: request-id 01F8-canary -> scores [0.63,0.81,0.59], request-id 01DF-stable -> scores [0.92,0.75,0.48].
Ben Ortiz: Ok thanks. ML — can you check if our reranker applies per-batch normalization or softmax differently between quantized and fp16 paths? Those can flip relative scores.
Jamal Reed: I pulled the logs from canary nodes. Two findings: 1) The candidate concatenation order was same. 2) There was a fallback to a different tokenizer shard (tokenizer-v3) on one canary host due to cache miss. Tokenizer difference could explain small score deltas but not typically >0.2. Also there is a per-request temperature override accidentally set to 1.1 in the canary config for rerank-service.
Sara Martinez: Whoa — temperature on reranker? That seems wrong. The config diff shows default temp() parameter changed in canary configpatch: `temperature: ${env.RERANK_TEMP:-1.1}` was accidentally committed. It should be 1e-6 (ie effectively deterministic).
Alyssa Chen: That would absolutely explain instability — rerank models use score calibration, a higher temperature will rescale logits and change softmax ordering. Great catch.
Ben Ortiz: Action plan: 1) Rollback canary to rerank-v2.1.2 on shard us-west-2-c, 2) remove the bad env default and push patch to canary config, 3) run golden-query regression harness (50k queries) across quant/fp paths and tokenizer variants.
Deploy Bot: "Rollback triggered: rerank-v2.1.2 rolled out to shard us-west-2-c (target success)" :white_check_mark:
Acme Support: After rollback our sample scores back to [0.92,0.75,0.48]. Thanks. We'll keep monitoring.
Jamal Reed: Follow-ups for ML team: check quant path calibration and add an automated check that blocks deploys if any environment defaults change core scoring params (temperature/scale). Also add a smoke test that compares top-1 overlap on a 500-query golden set before canary -> if top-1 overlap < 95% fail the deploy.
Sara Martinez: I'll file infra ticket INF-1827 to enforce env-var policy and another ML ticket ML-998 for calibration tests.
Alyssa Chen: I'll update the customer with a short RCA: accidental env default changed temperature in canary + tokenizer shard mismatch on one host; rollback done; working on test/guard rails; will run full regression and share SLA impact numbers.
Acme Support: Appreciated. Please include timeline and whether billing for affected calls will be credited (they saw a spike in reorders).
Ben Ortiz: I'll loop in finance for credits. Tagging @Sara and @Jamal for next steps. :thumbsup:
Alyssa Chen: Thanks team. Keeping thread open until regression harness passes and ML/Infra tickets closed.
